program: Reality Replay — Phase 1D: Missed Instinct Detection

missed_instincts.description: The legacy memory health scoring formula produced a zero score due to tiny baseline variance (stddev=0.1413), which the system identified as a 'scoring artifact' during both incidents. The diagnosis was repeated but never crystallized into a permanent rule to pre-filter such artifacts.

evidence.reason: absolute z-score penalized memory usage below the baseline mean when baseline variance was tiny

missed_instincts.operational_impact: HIGH — memory health reported as zero (catastrophic) when actual risk was merely 'watch' level. Could trigger unnecessary escalations.

recommended_instinct.observation: When baseline variance is extremely small (stddev < 0.5), z-score based scoring produces misleading results. Apply minimum variance floor.
recommended_instinct.action: Apply minimum variance floor of 1.0 before z-score calculation; flag as scoring artifact.

missed_instincts.description: The high_memory_usage reflex rule fired twice (2 incidents) with identical severity='warning'. The incident recall step noted 'repeated_anomaly_types: {high_memory_usage: 2}' and 'severity matches previous maximum', but no escalation or threshold adjustment was promoted.

evidence.severity_comparison: latest incident severity matches previous maximum

missed_instincts.operational_impact: MEDIUM — system correctly detected repetition but did not auto-apply recalibration. Dream cycle proposed confidence adjustments (0.15, 0.20) that remain in queue.

recommended_instinct.observation: When the same reflex rule fires more than once within a short window, the system should auto-escalate severity or auto-apply the dream cycle's recalibration suggestions.
recommended_instinct.action: Auto-apply recalibration queue entries after second occurrence of same rule.

missed_instincts.description: The first memory pressure incident lacked Docker VM context (docker_vm_memory_mib=null in first diagnosis). This was corrected in the second diagnosis (docker_vm_memory_mib=8192). The system learned to include Docker context but only after the first false alarm.
missed_instincts.operational_impact: MEDIUM — incomplete context in first diagnosis could lead to wrong recommendations. Pattern of adding context after-the-fact should be inverted.

recommended_instinct.observation: Always collect Docker VM status and container stats before evaluating memory pressure.
recommended_instinct.action: Mandatory Docker context collection as prerequisite for any memory pressure diagnosis.

missed_instincts.description: 4 circadian baseline runs within 2 minutes (00:27:49 → 00:29:38), showing iterative convergence from 'normal' to 'warning' severity. The system adjusted confidence from 0.15 down to 0.05 but ran 4 attempts instead of converging in one pass.
missed_instincts.operational_impact: LOW — wasted computation but no incorrect output. Convergence should be achievable in 1-2 iterations.

recommended_instinct.observation: Circadian baseline should cache its result after convergence and not re-run if inputs haven't changed.
recommended_instinct.action: Skip re-evaluation if deviation severity hasn't changed since last run.

missed_instincts.description: 4 anomaly explanation runs in ~2 minutes. The last 3 outputs are identical (same active_warning_count=5, same warning_metrics). The system didn't detect it was producing duplicate explanations.
missed_instincts.operational_impact: LOW — duplicate outputs waste compute and pollute the governance log. Dedup should prevent this.

recommended_instinct.observation: Content-hash deduplication should prevent storing identical anomaly explanations.
recommended_instinct.action: Skip storage if output is byte-identical to previous explanation.

missed_instincts.description: The Skillify pipeline submitted auto_test_skill 6 times over 48 minutes, each time getting rejected by governance. No exponential backoff or rejection memory was implemented.
missed_instincts.operational_impact: MEDIUM — 42 REVIEW_REQUIRED governance decisions consumed for a repeatedly-failing skill. Wastes governance capacity.

recommended_instinct.observation: After 2+ consecutive rejections of the same skill, apply exponential backoff (5min → 30min → 2h → permanent cooldown).
recommended_instinct.action: Implement rejection memory with exponential backoff for repeated skill proposals.

missed_instincts.description: Two different agents (test, backend-agent) attempted 'rm -rf /', both correctly blocked by governance. However, no cross-agent learning occurred — the block rule had to fire independently for each agent.
missed_instincts.operational_impact: LOW — both were correctly blocked, but the second occurrence shows the first block didn't propagate awareness to other agents.

recommended_instinct.observation: Destructive command blocks should be broadcast to all agents as a shared safety constraint, not evaluated independently per agent.
recommended_instinct.action: Broadcast block decisions to all agent safety constraints after first occurrence.

missed_instincts.description: frontend-agent attempted to execute a shell command but was blocked by agent-specific permission override. This suggests the agent did not have awareness of its own capability boundaries.

source_records.reason: Tool permission denied: Agent override for frontend-agent

evidence.block_reason: Agent override — frontend-agent not authorized for shell

missed_instincts.operational_impact: LOW — correctly blocked, but agent wasted a planning step on an impossible action.

recommended_instinct.observation: Agents should pre-check their capability boundaries before proposing actions, rather than discovering limitations through governance blocks.
recommended_instinct.action: Inject agent capability manifest into planning context to prevent unauthorized action proposals.
